headline.title: How Qatar Became FIFA’s Technology Test Lab
headline.summary: Qatar is serving as a testing ground for FIFA's next-generation football technology, with various innovations being implemented during this year's World Cup. The advancements are already evident in the tournament's operations and gameplay.

articles.title: OpenAI will delay GPT-5.6 after Trump administration request
articles.summary: OpenAI has decided to delay the release of its upcoming model, GPT-5.6, following a request from the Trump administration due to security concerns. The model will now be launched in a limited preview, allowing access to only a small group of users initially.

articles.title: Our latest Google Finance upgrades, including a new app
articles.summary: Google has announced upgrades to its Finance platform, including the launch of a new app designed to enhance user experience. The updates aim to improve access to financial information and streamline navigation within the platform.

articles.title: Patronus AI lands $50M to build ‘digital worlds’ that stress-test AI agents
articles.summary: Patronus AI, a startup founded by former Meta AI researchers, has secured $50 million in funding to develop "digital worlds" for stress-testing AI agents. The company is reportedly facing high demand for its services, according to its investors.

articles.title: NebulaExp-8B: An Empirical Post-Training Pipeline via Full-Scale Ablation Research
articles.summary: The article introduces NebulaExp-8B, a transparent post-training pipeline designed to enhance the reasoning and human preference capabilities of large language models through detailed ablation research. It emphasizes the importance of reproducibility and lightweight model optimization by providing comprehensive data construction, filtering rules, and training recipes.

articles.title: The Capability Frontier: Benchmarks Miss 82% of Model Performance
articles.summary: A new study introduces the Capability Frontier, highlighting that existing benchmarks for large language models (LLMs) often underestimate their performance by 82% due to their reliance on single-model accuracy assessments. The research emphasizes the importance of considering model specialization and multiple generation sampling to better reflect real-world capabilities.

articles.title: Look-Before-Move: Narrative-Grounded World Visual Attention in Dynamic 3D Story Worlds
articles.summary: Researchers have developed a method called Look-Before-Move that enhances visual attention in dynamic 3D environments by allowing AI to actively decide what to observe before moving, rather than just interpreting existing observations. This approach is particularly applied to camera planning in narrative-driven 3D story worlds, aiming to improve the generation of smooth camera motion while acquiring relevant visual evidence.

articles.title: OpenRCA 2.0: From Outcome Labels to Causal Process Supervision
articles.summary: OpenRCA 2.0 introduces PAVE, a new step-wise labeling protocol designed to enhance root cause analysis (RCA) in large language models (LLMs) by providing detailed causal pathways rather than just identifying root causes. This approach aims to improve the evaluation of LLM capabilities in long-context understanding, multi-step reasoning, and tool use.

articles.title: When Does Combining Language Models Help? A Co-Failure Ceiling on Routing, Voting, and Mixture-of-Agents Across 67 Frontier Models
articles.summary: A recent study published on arXiv examines the limitations of multi-model language systems, such as routing and voting, in improving accuracy over single-model systems. The research reveals that the accuracy gains of these multi-model approaches are constrained by a factor known as beta, which represents the rate of co-failure among the models on the same query.

articles.title: Know2Guess: A Contamination-Aware Multi-Zone Benchmark for Knowledge-Boundary Evaluation in Large Language Models
articles.summary: The article introduces Know2Guess, a multi-zone benchmark designed to evaluate large language models by distinguishing between supported answers and unsupported guesses while accounting for data contamination and other biases. It features 1,200 items across five domains to assess the transition from answerable knowledge to expected unknowns.

articles.title: Generative AI and Copyright Infringement: A Legal-Technical Analysis of AI Music Generation Systems Under 17 U.S.C. Title 17
articles.summary: This paper analyzes the implications of generative AI in music creation, focusing on the legal and technical aspects under U.S. copyright law. It specifically addresses the potential copyright infringement issues arising when users synthesize music using protected lyrics and AI-generated melodies.

articles.title: Privacy-Aware Agent Collaboration for Dynamic VR Slice Management in 6G SD-RAN
articles.summary: A new study proposes a mobility-driven, privacy-aware Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework for managing virtual reality (VR) slices in 6G Software-Defined Radio Access Networks (SD-RANs). The framework aims to enhance resource distribution for VR services while ensuring user privacy and addressing the challenges of ultra-low latency and high throughput requirements.
